findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (member vote: Aye, 66 to 47)
findings.note: HB 958 is a broad election law bill. Its text includes photo ID rules: a voter whose driver license or Social Security number does not match at registration must show ID with the ballot, in person or absentee; a voter without photo ID may cast a provisional ballot and must present ID by a deadline; absentee request forms carry ID information. Same day the member voted Aye on amendment A1 (Blackwell, 112 to 0) and Aye on amendment A2 (Blackwell, 69 to 44), and No on amendment A3 (Dahle, failed 47 to 66). Contents of the amendments were not read.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (vote to agree with Senate changes; member vote: Aye, 62 to 47)
findings.note: Final House vote to concur on HB 958, sending it on. The bill page shows the Governor vetoed it on 08/17/2026 (https://www.ncleg.gov/BillLookUp/2025/H958). No override vote was found on the member's vote list at fetch time.

House vote to concur in the Senate committee substitute of HB 958, Election Law Changes (roll call 2026-08-04, 6:26 PM): Humphrey voted Aye, 62 to 47. The ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) adds G.S. 163-83, under which a county board processes a registration application only if it affirmatively says the applicant is a U.S. citizen. A blank answer gets a notice, and a statement under penalty of perjury is required within 30 days. It also bars driver-license-office staff from proceeding with a registration unless the applicant says they are a citizen, and it requires a process to remove voters flagged as non-citizens in a federal database. The bill page shows the bill was vetoed 2026-08-17.
subjects: voter-roll checks and removal of non-citizens
